title: An Asynchronous 160×90 Flash LiDAR Sensor with Dynamic Frame Rates of 5 to 250fps Based on Pixelwise ToF Validation via a Background-Light-Adaptive Threshold
problem: Flash LiDAR sensors require large on-chip histogramming time-to-digital converters (hTDC) for time-correlated single-photon counting, constrained by physical size and impacting spatial resolution; frame-based sensors suffer suboptimal frame rates tied to worst-case pixel SNR, and background light intensity severely degrades conventional designs.
method: Asynchronous event-driven readout scheme with pixelwise ToF validation and background-light-adaptive threshold dynamically adjusts pixel sensitivity and event rate control. On-chip histogramming with intelligent pixel-level filtering enables 5–250fps dynamic frame rates. Architecture combines time-gated photon counting with spiking neuron-like event generation and integrated control logic for on-chip sensitivity adaptation.

title: 35.2 A Spatial-Domain Compressive-Sensing Photoacoustic Imager with Matrix-Multiplying SAR ADC
problem: Wearable deep-tissue photoacoustic (PA) imaging requires low-power, compact receive architecture with integrated data compression for real-time streaming and long-term monitoring, but PA signals are 10x smaller than ultrasound due to optical excitation inefficiency.
method: A spatial-domain compressive-sensing receiver architecture with matrix-multiplying SAR ADC performs simultaneous signal acquisition and compression at the sensor level. The SAR ADC computes matrix-vector products during conversion, implementing spatial sampling and measurement in hardware. Optimized for PA's low signal amplitude by tuning gain, bandwidth, and noise characteristics.

title: 10.3 A D-Band 2D-Scalable 4×4 Active Reflective Relay with Orthogonally Polarized on-Chip TX/RX Antennas and in-Front-End Common-Centroid Fast Azimuth/Elevation Angle-of-Arrival Detection
problem: mm-Wave and sub-THz NLOS links require reflective relay arrays to overcome line-of-sight (LOS) blockage, but existing relays operate open-loop without on-the-fly angle-of-arrival (AoA) detection; prior AoA methods either require lossy down-/up-mixers, continuously tunable phase shifters with stability concerns, or narrow AoA range.
method: A 4×4 D-band active reflective relay integrates orthogonally polarized TX/RX on-chip antennas and implements in-front-end common-centroid fast AoA detection (both azimuth and elevation). The relay detects incident beam angles and steers the output beam adaptively without requiring lossy mixers or tunable phase shifter loops.

title: Efficient Caching with A Tag-enhanced DRAM
problem: DRAM-based caches (e.g., HBM3-as-cache) suffer from high miss penalties due to two-step tag-then-data access, wasted data movement on cache misses where data is fetched then discarded, and interference between demand requests and miss-fetched data on the data bus. Existing DRAM cache designs cannot perform in-DRAM tag comparison or conditional data response, so they always transfer data regardless of hit/miss status.
method: TDRAM adds small, low-latency metadata/tag mats to an HBM3 die alongside the existing data mats, enabling lockstep tag-and-data access, in-DRAM tag comparison, and conditional data response (data is only transferred to the CPU if the comparison indicates a hit), eliminating wasted data bus transfers on misses. Opportunistic early tag probing allows tag lookups to start before the full row is available, reducing both hit and miss latencies. A flush buffer stores conflicting dirty data on write misses within the DRAM, eliminating data bus turnaround delays caused by writing back dirty evictees before fetching new data.

title: A 96fsrms-Jitter, -70.6dBc-Fractional-Spur Cascaded PLL Employing Two MMDs with Shared DSM for Quantization Noise Cancellation
problem: Fractional-N PLLs suffer from quantization noise (Q-noise) and fractional spurs from the delta-sigma modulator (DSM). Existing quantization-error cancellation (QEC) approaches require intensive calibration with long settling times; multi-PLL architectures introduce mixing spurs requiring bulky analog filters; cascaded integer-fractional approaches leave fractional spurs in-band at near-integer channels.
method: A cascaded PLL architecture employs two multi-modulus dividers (MMDs) sharing a single DSM for quantization noise cancellation. By operating the shared DSM at elevated frequency, Q-noise is pushed out of bandwidth and filtered naturally, while the dual-MMD structure suppresses fractional spurs in-band through noise subtraction without requiring intensive digital calibration.

title: AutoSkewBMT: Autonomously Synthesizing Optimized Integrity Authentication Mechanism for DNN Accelerators
problem: DNN accelerators require memory security (encryption and integrity authentication) to protect data, but standard approaches like Bonsai Merkle Tree (BMT) integrity checks incur prohibitive overhead in high-throughput accelerator workloads, creating a bottleneck between security and performance.
method: AutoSkewBMT autonomously generates optimized BMT configurations by skewing the tree structure to match specific DNN workload access patterns; uses a novel design space generation algorithm to explore tree geometries and selects the configuration maximizing throughput while maintaining cryptographic integrity guarantees.

title: Reviving In-Storage Hardware Compression on ZNS SSDs through Host-SSD Collaboration
problem: Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs cannot benefit from traditional host-transparent in-storage hardware compression because the ZNS interface's sequential write constraint makes it impossible to locate variable-length compressed chunks and reclaim the space freed by compression without exposing this information to the host.
method: CCZNS (Collaborative Compression for ZNS) decouples compression execution from indexing by introducing a new ZNS interface extension where the SSD hardware performs compression but exposes chunk boundaries and offset metadata to the host rather than hiding them. The host (e.g., RocksDB with ZenFS) uses this metadata to manage address mapping and space reclamation, while the SSD accelerates the compression compute. A case study on RocksDB/ZenFS demonstrates how the host software is adapted to consume CCZNS metadata.

title: NDFT: Accelerating Density Functional Theory Calculations via Hardware/Software Co-Design on Near-Data Computing System
problem: Linear-response time-dependent DFT (LR-TDDFT) is memory-bound with constant data movement between host and heterogeneous accelerators (GPU, FPGA, Sunway), creating substantial data movement overhead that dominates compute-optimized kernels.
method: NDFT proposes a near-data processing (NDP) framework that partitions LR-TDDFT tasks across CPU and NDP units optimally, offloading each computation phase to the most suitable processing element. Critical kernels undergo hardware/software co-optimization on the CPU-NDP system to further reduce data movement and latency.

title: 9.4 A 102ns/V 94.3%-Peak-Efficiency Symbol-Power-Tracking Supply Modulator for 5G NR Power Amplifiers
problem: 5G power amplifiers require symbol-level power tracking to match instantaneous transmit power, but achieving fast voltage transitions (102ns/V) within cyclic prefix duration (1.17µs) while maintaining efficiency remains challenging.
method: Symbol-power-tracking supply modulator using split-capacitor topology with direct switching converter and auxiliary circuits to achieve 102ns/V tracking speed and 94.3% dynamic efficiency within brief cyclic-prefix intervals.

title: KLiNQ: Knowledge Distillation-Assisted Lightweight Neural Network for Qubit Readout on FPGA
problem: Qubit readout in superconducting quantum processors is slow and error-prone; current neural-network approaches require large, resource-intensive models and lack support for mid-circuit measurements critical for quantum error correction.
method: KLiNQ uses knowledge distillation to compress neural networks to 99% smaller size while maintaining 91% qubit-state discrimination accuracy. Each qubit gets a dedicated compact neural network on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA, enabling independent 32-ns readouts.

title: SuperFast: Fast Supernet Training Using Initial Knowledge
problem: Once-for-all neural architecture search supernet training requires extremely high computational cost (72-83+ GPU days), limiting practical applicability despite enabling efficient multi-target deployment.
method: SuperFast employs two-stage training: (1) pretrains a small subnet within the supernet search space, (2) distributes this subnet's learned knowledge across the full supernet before main training. Knowledge propagation from small to large models enables faster convergence and better accuracy-cost tradeoffs. Plug-and-play workflow compatible with ElasticViT and NASViT.

title: 17.2 A 28nm 4.05µJ/Encryption 8.72kHMul/s Reconfigurable Multi-Scheme Fully Homomorphic Encryption Processor for Encrypted Client-Server Computing
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving machine learning but incurs prohibitive power consumption and fabrication costs for bootstrapping operations; supporting multiple FHE schemes (BGV, BFV, CKKS) and diverse client/server primitives while managing intensive memory bottlenecks remains challenging.
method: The 28nm FHE processor implements reconfigurable architecture supporting BGV, BFV, and CKKS schemes with optimized primitives for both client and server computation patterns; architecture-circuit co-optimizations address (I)NTT and polynomial automorphism overhead while managing on-chip data movement.

title: Self-Attention to Operator Learning-based 3D-IC Thermal Simulation
problem: Efficient thermal simulation for 3D ICs with high power densities; traditional PDE-solving methods are accurate but computationally slow for iterative design workflows.
method: Self-Attention UNet Fourier Neural Operator (SAU-FNO) combines self-attention mechanisms with U-Net architecture and FNO to capture long-range dependencies and model local high-frequency features effectively. Transfer learning fine-tunes low-fidelity training data to reduce dependence on extensive high-fidelity datasets and accelerate training.

title: Anda: Unlocking Efficient LLM Inference with a Variable-Length Grouped Activation Data Format
problem: Weight-only quantized LLMs retain floating-point (FP) activations for accuracy, which shifts the energy and latency bottleneck to costly FP memory accesses and FP-INT GEMM computation; existing LLM accelerators optimize computation alone without jointly addressing data representation and movement for FP activations.
method: Anda proposes a new adaptive activation data type with a group-shared exponent and dynamically allocated mantissa bits per group, enabling variable precision per LLM module. An iterative post-training precision search algorithm determines per-module bit-widths to balance accuracy and efficiency without retraining. On the hardware side, Anda uses a bit-plane-based data organization, bit-serial computation processing elements, and a runtime bit-plane compressor to simultaneously shrink storage, computation, and memory footprint. The result is a hardware-software co-designed accelerator targeting FP-INT GEMM in LLMs.

title: ChipletEM: Physics-Based 2.5D and 3D Chiplet Heterogeneous Integration Electromigration Signoff Tool Using Coupled Stress and Thermal Simulation
problem: Electromigration (EM) in 2.5D/3D chiplet heterogeneous integration systems is inadequately understood; existing EM research ignores Through Silicon Vias (TSVs) and non-uniform thermal distribution between dies, causing signoff errors and missing critical failure modes.
method: ChipletEM couples electrical-thermal simulation using finite volume method (FVM) for initial temperature and current density in TSVs, finite difference time domain (FDTD) solver for hydrostatic stress (nucleation and post-voiding), thermal migration effects, and analytical TSV thermal solver. Components are coupled at each timestep to simulate interactions between EM stress, thermal stress, void growth, resistance change, IR drop, and Joule heating.

title: Query-Based Black-Box Stealthy Sensor Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems
problem: Designing stealthy sensor attacks on cyber-physical systems under black-box conditions (minimal knowledge of target system) requires maintaining attack stealthiness both in output (avoiding detector alerts) and during attack generation (limiting detector queries).
method: Query-based black-box attack framework using active learning to extract detector information into a time series model without triggering alerts. The framework maintains stealthiness during training via adaptive query budgeting and generates attack sequences from the learned model that bypass CPS safety constraints.
